title: AgentPO: Enhancing Multi-Agent Collaboration via Reinforcement Learning
claim: One RL-trained collaborator agent generates auxiliary signals that plug into diverse fixed multi-agent topologies and is optimized with group-relative rewards.
layout: 4 stacked panels: GRPO flow on top, three topology variants below, left-to-right
description: The figure has two main parts. The top row is a left-to-right GRPO training pipeline. Grouped inputs i1..iG go through an Actor Agent to outputs o1..oG. A Reward Model and a Reference box feed rewards r1..rG, then a Group Computation box produces advantages A1..AG. Each group is drawn as a grey rounded container with stacked white cells. A connector runs from the input group to dashed panels below. These show the collaborator in different topologies. Panels (a) Feed-forward Mode and (b) Feedback Mode are two-agent topologies with a Hint Agent or Critic Agent. Panels (c) Multi-Agent Debate and (d) Role Assignment are multi-agent topologies with robot icons. The trainable collaborator is orange with a flame icon, and the frozen actors are blue. A circled C marks concatenation of the question q.
caption: Our proposed AgentPO framework enhances multi-agent system performance through collaborative optimization. Given a problem, auxiliary signal is generated by the collaborator, which depends on the topology structure: the Hint Agent in the Feed-forward Mode, the Critic Agent in the Feedback Mode or the Collaborator in the Multi-Agents Topology. This auxiliary signal is then concatenated with the original problem to form the input for the Actor Agent. The Collaborator’s parameters are subsequently optimized using the GRPO algorithm.
abstract: Multi-Agent Systems (MAS) offer a powerful paradigm for solving complex problems through distributed reasoning and collaboration. However, their effectiveness is often hindered by the challenge of optimizing interactions among agents. To address this, we introduce AgentPO, a novel framework that directly optimizes agent collaboration. AgentPO employs reinforcement learning to train a specialized Collaborator agent, which refines its interaction policy to enhance overall system performance within a fixed multi-agent topology. We evaluated AgentPO on multiple mathematical reasoning tasks, where it consistently outperformed strong baselines. With Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct as the actor model, AgentPO achieves accuracy improvements of +1.8\% and +7.2\% over strong baselines like Role Assignment and EvoAgent, respectively. When using the larger Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model, these gains increase to +5.6\% and +11.3\%. Crucially, AgentPO achieves these results with remarkable efficiency: it requires only 500 training samples and operates at just 7.8\% of EvoAgent's inference cost, highlighting its superior scalability and practicality.
